title: Private canary evaluator for customer config/model changes with policy-driven redaction
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: provide customers on Dedicated/Private deployments an automated, per-customer canary evaluator that runs ephemeral eval jobs inside customer-controlled environments (VPC or on-prem), validates model/config changes against local golden sets, and exports only privacy-safe rollup metrics to Redwood Console. The canary evaluator must: run on config or model version transitions, honor tenant data isolation and redaction policies, use customer-managed encryption keys (KMS/HSM) for golden sets and intermediate artifacts, and tie into rollout policies to permit automatic rollback or progressive promotion based on configurable thresholds.

Why: customers have told us they need deterministic, private validation of model/config changes before switching production routing. Hosted/global evals leak provenance and cannot operate on sensitive local goldens. This feature reduces rollout risk and supports compliance requirements for regulated customers.

Non-goals: not intended to replace centralized benchmarking or large-scale offline evals; not required for free-hosted tier customers.

Success metrics: reduction in post-rollout regressions for private tenants by 60% within first 3 months; adoption by 25% of Dedicated customers within 6 months; median canary job runtime <20m for 1k-sample golden set (initial SLI).
acceptance_criteria: Canary evaluator can be triggered automatically on model/config change in the control plane
Evaluator pod runs inside tenant VPC or customer on-prem execution host and does not send raw outputs to Redwood telemetry by default
Customer-managed KMS keys used for encrypting golden sets and artifacts; Redwood only sees encrypted blobs unless customer opts-in
Configurable policy-driven redaction executes client-side (in-tenant) to scrub PII before any artifact leaves the tenant boundary
Console shows privacy-safe rollup metrics (diffs, regression flags, confidence bands) and links to customer-side run artifacts without exposing raw text
Automatic gating: when a regression threshold is exceeded the rollout pauses and optional rollback executes per tenant rollout policy
comments: 2026-02-13 — PM kickoff: scoped initial MVP to support text-generation models and small golden sets (<=2k examples). Shared PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVAL/PM-90234-Private-Canary-Evaluator

2026-02-25 — Eng sync (Diego): ENG-44122 will provide the tenant-side runner image and secure execution harness. Need trait-based RBAC hooks from ENG-45190. Blocking until ENG-44122 image artifact is publishable to customer registries.

2026-03-01 — Security review (Priya): client-side redaction library must be FIPS-compatible for regulated customers. Proposed design: pluggable redactors and regex+model-based scrubbers running inside tenant boundary. Action: schedule threat model review w/ Security 2026-03-05.
2026-03-04 — Design feedback (Maya): Console UX needs a compact canary timeline and clear 'data not exported' badges. Added DES-204 for mockups. Figma links: https://figma.com/file/xyz/canary-console

2026-03-08 — Decision: initial telemetry export will be numeric aggregates (per-metric histograms, delta scores, boolean regression flags). No raw tokens or prompts will be exported unless customer explicitly opts into 'golden-share' with a signed consent flow.

2026-03-09 — Ops note (Sam): ephemeral canary jobs should default to resource limits that reflect Dedicated/NVIDIA A10p baseline; autoscale policy for canary parallelism gated by tenant capacity and dedicated pool size.

2026-03-10 — PM follow-up: update PRD with rollout policy presets (strict, moderate, permissive) and include examples for enterprise customers. Next milestone: implementation spike by ENG to prove in-VPC runner and KMS integration (target 2026-03-24).
implementation_notes: Runner: a small containerized evaluator shipped as a signed image customers can pull into their registries. It mounts customer KMS/HSM via provider plugins (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault, on-prem HSM connectors).

Dataflow: golden set stored encrypted in tenant storage; evaluator decrypts locally, runs comparisons, computes aggregates; only aggregates are sent to Redwood via a TLS channel with mutual auth and policy attestations.

Redaction: provide SDK adapters for customer-preferred redaction rules; default library uses token-level heuristics + lightweight ML-based PII detection with local models to avoid sending sensitive spans off-host.
Rollout integration: integrate with Console rollout engine so canary pass/fail feeds routing decisions. Provide API hooks for customers to override thresholds and choose automatic rollback semantics.
Observability: tenant-only logs persisted to customer storage; Redwood Console will surface run metadata plus numeric traces (latency, token-efficiency, regression score) but no verbatim outputs.

Trade-offs: tighter privacy (no raw export) reduces our ability to debug model diffs centrally and may increase time-to-resolution for platform ops. We will provide optional 'escrowed' artifact-sharing flows under explicit consent.

Performance: initial quant targets for canary runs: 1k-example golden set completes within 20 minutes on baseline resources. If customers need larger suites, document cost and time trade-offs and suggest sampling/stratified probes.
Compliance: required artifacts for audits include signed attestations of where processing occurred and KMS logs; coordinate with Security to generate standard audit bundles.
Metrics schema: regression_score (float), delta_accuracy (float), percentile_latency_ms (p50,p95), token_cost_estimate (float), pass_bool (true/false).
